security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, if the load/store unit (LSU) or page table walker (PTW) incorrectly applies the pointer masking ignore transformation to implicit memory accesses (page table walks, instruction fetches from I$, cache line refills), the hardware would use masked/tagged addresses for page table entry lookups instead of the true physical addresses. This occurs when the PM-enable signal from the CSR module (senvcfg.PMM, menvcfg.PMM, mseccfg.PMM) is not properly gated by an 'is_explicit_access' qualifier in the address generation pipeline, allowing the ignore transformation to propagate into PTW requests, instruction fetch addresses, or SFENCE/HFENCE/SINVAL/HINVAL operations. Specifically, if the Chisel code in the LSU's address computation stage applies the mask ({PMLEN{sign_bit}, addr_lower}) or ({PMLEN{1'b0}, addr_lower}) unconditionally when PM is enabled, without checking that the access is an explicit load/store/atomic rather than a page walk or instruction fetch, this constitutes a spec violation of norm:pm_not_apply_implicit.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: PointerMasking(enable && !isExplicit) || pm_apply && (isPTW || isIFetch || isCMO || isSFENCE) || ignore_transform && io.valid && !checkExplicit
security_spec.summary: Pointer masking ignore transform applied to implicit accesses (PTW, I-fetch, fence ops) instead of only explicit loads/stores/atomics — breaks virtual memory isolation by allowing tagged addresses in page table walks
